To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sinusoidal perfusion of livers is heterogeneous during HMP, and this is associated with morphological changes in the endothelial cell structures.
heterogeneous flow pattern, stasis and morphological changes in sinusoidal endothelial cells occur during 24h hypothermic machine preservation, which may lead the tissue to fail after reperfusion.
the heterogeneous flow pattern, the red cell stasis and the edema occur during extended HMP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the flow dynamics and the structure of endothelial cells in the liver sinusoid after 24-h hypothermic machine preservation with UW solution.
the flow dynamics and ECs structures in livers during extended HMP.
the flow dynamics and EC structure during 24h cold HMP preservation of livers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the major cause of HMP injury is heterogeneous flow and stasis, which may be due to the morphological changes of ECs.
sinusoidal flow dynamics and endothelium structure are important factors that determine the success of HMP preservation of livers, especially for extended preservation.
the morphological changes in endothelial structures are a major cause of preservation failure during 24h cold HMP of livers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current preservation solution is not adequate for long term perfusion preservation of liver.
HMP preservation may enhance donor organ pool by extending preservation times and reclaiming marginal organs including those from non-beating donors.
sinusoidal stasis is a major cause of preservation failure in livers during HMP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HMP preservation of liver may be improved by understanding the flow dynamics and EC structures during HMP.

the flow heterogeneity and red cell stasis observed during HMP is caused by morphological changes of the ECs, leading to sinusoidal obstruction, which is the main cause of the preservation injury during HMP preservation of livers.
